name: Driftpile Acidwalk Full Kit
description: Built around a rubberized poncho-coat in matte black that has long since faded to an uneven charcoal, this outfit is a Shelf rain-walker's solution to the Great Lakes acid season. The poncho-coat reaches mid-thigh, its hem patched in four places with strips of bright yellow hazard tape that the wearer has made no attempt to hide — they're functional and they're a statement. Beneath it, a dense-knit compression top in dark teal, faded nearly to gray at the shoulders, sits tucked into wide-leg work trousers in heavyweight stained canvas, olive-brown, with a drawstring waist because the original button hardware gave out. The trousers have a gene-compatible rear seam — split and re-hemmed with elastic to accommodate a tail or lower-back geneware — suggesting the wearer either has modifications or bought the trousers secondhand from someone who did. Boots are tall and utilitarian: knee-high salvage pulls in cracked synthetic leather, resoled with thick rubber compound that smells faintly of chemical treatment, the inner lining replaced with cut-up foam insulation. Hands are covered by fingerless gloves in worn leather, the knuckles patched with embedded rubber nodes stripped from industrial grip-tape. A wide-brimmed hat in stiff waxed canvas, acid-pocked but holding shape, completes the silhouette — shaped and battered into a permanent slight lean to one side.
functionality: Rubberized poncho-coat sheds acid rain and light chemical splash. Tall synthetic boots protect lower legs from flood-water and chemical runoff. Grip-tape knuckle gloves improve hold on wet or slick surfaces. Wide-brimmed hat keeps acid rain off face and neck. Gene-compatible trouser seam accommodates tail-bearing wearers.
what_it_says: Someone who moves through the Shelf's worst weather conditions regularly and has engineered their wardrobe to survive it. The yellow hazard tape hem is defiant — practical necessity worn like a badge. The secondhand gene-compatible trousers suggest a community that shares and adapts.
manufacturer: Poncho-coat is a Floodline industrial surplus second; remaining components are self-modified or sourced from Shelf market vendors
story_hooks: The chemical treatment on the boot resoles is a proprietary formula the wearer mixed themselves — and a Tier 3 materials chemist has noticed it's better than anything commercially available.
The gene-compatible trouser seam is stitched in a specific pattern that marks the wearer as belonging to a particular Shelf mutual-aid collective — which makes them a target for a rival group.
During a sudden acid downpour, the wearer is the only person on the street prepared to move safely — and someone desperate needs an escort to the nearest shelter.
